video_title: Will The Wizards Trade Anthony Davis Before Deadline?

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating the likelihood of a Wizards or Jazz roster flip
quotes.excerpt: Which do you think is more likely, these two scenarios?

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Let me ask you this, Windy. Which do you think is more likely, these two scenarios? One, on March 1st, the Washington Wizards have a W, a winning record, and I got to call them the Wizards again. Or, number two, on March 1st, Anthony Davis is playing somewhere else.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: It's a great question. I don't think they're going to have a winning record on March 1st. So, I can't say that that, you know. The Anthony Davis thing is fascinating because he's had some games this year where he's looked spectacular.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The central question surrounding Anthony Davis and the Wizards
quotes.excerpt: Whatever one's wanting to know is, are they going to trade him or not?
quotes.quote: Whatever one's wanting to know is, are they going to trade him or not? Now, the other thing that people are watching is if the Wizards contemplate a coaching change, and whether or not this poor start will result in a coaching change, and if there's a coaching change, whether or not that would buy them a reset.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Phil Jackson likely wouldn't save the struggling Wizards
quotes.excerpt: I think you can get Phil Jackson at his absolute peak to come to Washington and they're still not going to be a winning team.
quotes.quote: I think you can get Phil Jackson at his absolute peak to come to Washington and they're still not going to be a winning team.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The Wizards face a difficult trade or pay decision with Anthony Davis
quotes.excerpt: It's going to reach a point before the trade deadline where you got to make a decision and that's either trade him or pay him.
quotes.quote: The Anthony Davis thing, look, it's going to reach a point before the trade deadline where you got to make a decision and that's either trade him or pay him. And I think there's big problems with either of those scenarios. Because if you're paying him, unless there's a significant turnaround, you've got a really expensive team that needs to improve to reach mediocrity. That's not a good thing.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Anthony Davis opt out of his player option?
quotes.excerpt: Do we really believe that he is for sure not picking up his $63 million player option for next year?
quotes.quote: The interesting thing about Anthony Davis is, do we really believe that he is for sure not picking up his $63 million player option for next year?

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The financial reality of the Anthony Davis contract situation
quotes.excerpt: Because nobody wants to pay him.
quotes.quote: Because nobody wants to pay him. I'm sure somebody would pay him, but maybe not. The reason that you would turn that down is because you could get, I mean, he's going to be, I don't know if he is 33 or going to turn 33, this is his age 33 season. He still, I'm sure, believes he's got one big contract left.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The challenge of trading a player like Anthony Davis
quotes.excerpt: It's going to be hard to make a trade of Anthony Davis that's going to win any press conferences or impress your bosses.
quotes.quote: It's going to be hard to make a trade of Anthony Davis that's going to win any press conferences or impress your bosses. A guy like Anthony Davis, who's been an All-Star a ton of times, all-NBA, won a championship, is a sure-fire Hall of Famer. Guys like that, look at their $63 million player options, they say, yeah, you know what, I'm willing to take less. But less is in the 50s.
